Hi everyone,

I'm interested in formalising Statistics and - perhaps for a separate conversation - asking what that even means.

I'd like to start with t-test.

The linear regression model is probably the most useful general framework around this test, and I've got a basic lean proof that the ordinary least squares estimator is optimal.

What I need is to prove that it is asymptotically Gaussian; I've followed @Rémy Degenne 's CLT, but I think this isn't enough and I need:

  • The Lindeberg CLT
  • Slutsky's theorem

I think I might be able to do them, but just wanted to check first if this was already in someone's plans, and/or if anyone was interested in being involved.

Best wishes,
Patrick
I am not aware of any work towards the Lindeberg CLT.

If you work in a public repository, I'd be interested in following what you do, and perhaps give you some feedback from time to time. I'm interested in getting some statistics into Lean, but I'm already involved in too many other projects to also be really active in this one.
Great, thanks. I'll start by trying to get my head around how much work a Lindeberg CLT would potentially be, and report back.

The direct proof of the Lindenberg CLT using the Lindenberg method (which gives an alternative proof of the classical CLT) is one of my favorite proofs. However given that we have the classical CLT its likely much easier (and better for Mathlib) to use a proof that builds off the classical one. At a glance following the proof of Theorem 6.13 in Kallenbergs Foundations of Modern Probability seems quite doable.
Let me use this topic to attract attention to the PR that adds the final lines needed to actually have the CLT in Mathlib: #36208 (+163, -3). It needs review!

It's done! @Andy Jones and I have put a working version on https://github.com/patrickrd/CLT-lindeberg.

Some comments:

  • Much credit to @Rémy Degenne - given the the Levy continuity theorem (MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_tendsto_charFun) it pretty much just comes down establishing an analytical fact.
  • Although the proof is formalised, we're trying to make it nicer + easier - any comments welcome!
  • Moving towards a CLT for the linear model, turns out there are a few more problems to navigate; basically whether/how to use Slutsky versus extending the Lindeberg CLT to a triangular array version. Again, please reach out if you want to advise! (Or be involved.)
